content:
nina: Quick sync — we keep seeing GPU time mapped to the wrong tenant when requests are rerouted (fallback model/region) or when runtime batches mix tenants. Anyone tracked a pragmatic way to propagate a cost path that survives routing + batching?

ben: ugh yeah this has bitten billing. current pipeline only looks at the model-serving logs which are post-routing, so it loses the original route/route-owner in some fallthroughs.

priya: options: 1) propagate a small, immutable cost-header across the request path (hash tenant + route + cohort), 2) emit a lightweight route-event to a dedicated cost-collector service at ingress and join later, or 3) reconstruct via best-effort inference from final model logs.

matt: agree on the three. tradeoffs: header = immediate and accurate but increases header cardinality & surface area (edge proxies/logs), collector service = extra hop & availability concern, reconstruction = lossy.

nina: example header we were thinking (short):
```
X-RDW-COST: t=h(tenant:12345)|r=chat-guest|m=rw-v2|s=shard-03|b=grp-7
```
log line at GPU runtime: `gpu-serve[shard-03] process req id=abc123 cost=X-RDW-COST=t=...`

ben: I'd always hash tenant id (h(...)) so raw tenant doesn't leak in many logs. also consider bucketizing route names to reduce cardinality (chat-guest -> chat-01).

priya: +1 on hashing + bucketizing. also we should cap distinct batch ids kept in the header (we only need the batch-group id for attribution, not every request id).

matt: what about retries & fallbacks: if runtime reroutes to a cheaper model variant, do we keep original route in header or replace? For cost accounting I think original route should be preserved (who caused the request) but also record the final model variant used for GPU time split. so header should be append-only or we carry two fields: origin and effective.

nina: yeah, origin vs effective sounds right. header sample: `origin=...;effective=...`

ben: storage/query side: will we index X-RDW-COST verbatim? that could explode. keep a normalized mapping service: header -> small fingerprint id that we persist (fingerprint resolved to fields in a separate table). then cost queries join on fingerprint.

priya: that's basically the collector-service pattern but cheap: edge computes fingerprint (H1) and includes H1 in headers, the mapping table is populated asynchronously. avoids copying large strings in hot logs.

matt: operational cornercases: cross-region routing means fingerprint must be globally stable (same hash algo & bucket mapping everywhere). also handle clock skew if collector receives mapping after GPU logs. we need deterministic mapping algorithm.

nina: concern: cardinality spike during experiments or feature flags could create many fingerprints. mitigation: enforce rate limits and fallback to a "unknown-cohort" fingerprint when exceeded.

ben: metrics around this: emit a counting metric when we fallback to unknown-cohort so we can alert.

ops-bot: deploy-notice: test patch that adds X-RDW-COST header to router -> upstream in staging at 2024-11-02T14:05:20Z (build #rwd-obs-1123). Rolling to 10% traffic. :rotating_light:

nina: nice. next steps: Priya + Ben to draft short RFC describing header shape + hashing algo + mapping table schema; Matt to enumerate retry/fallback semantics and failure modes; I'll add an ops playbook for `unknown-cohort` alerting. Aim to have RFC by EOW.

priya: will do. starting doc now, will ping reviewers.

ben: I'll prototype the fingerprint resolver service and a small query join example.

matt: can we also add a short test in the integration harness simulating mixed-tenant batches so we can validate attribution before wide rollout?

nina: yes — add to org/integration/testcases/attr-mix.

ops-bot: staging tests enqueued (job 9876).

nina: thanks all. we'll take decisions in RFC but this thread captured the tradeoffs. :white_check_mark:
